rows.evidence: Q1: Abstract and Sections III-V describe the authors' own development of hardware (integrated sensor module, valve controllers, Raspberry medium-layer controller), server architecture and three scheduling/control modes, with software testing reported.
rows.notes: The study is an engineering/system-description paper; it reports no field trial, no crop yield or quality data and no drought conditions. Nothing in the text supports the claim that automated sensor-based systems maintained constant yield and quality under drought. Q1 is marginal: the paper presents a developed prototype and an example report diagram (Fig. 6) but no measured outcomes.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections III-V describe the authors' own design and implementation of the irrigation control platform and software testing.
rows.notes: No result on drought risk management, yield stability or quality. The paper only describes system architecture, control modes (closed-loop automated, semi-automatic open loop, manual) and reporting applications; the Introduction cites national strategy on climate adaptation but presents no own evidence.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections II-V and Conclusion report the authors' own development of a three-layer control platform integrating wind turbine/PV power, sensor modules, GPRS communication, two servers and reporting applications (Fig. 6 example report of irrigation norms, precipitation and volumes).
rows.notes: The study shows that the platform was built with renewable-energy integration and data visualization (Fig. 6), but it reports no measurement of water use or water savings attributable to the scheduling platform; 'efficient irrigation management' is asserted as a design goal, not demonstrated with data. The paper supports only the precondition (existence and functionality of the platform) for the claimed water-conservation effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Section III and Fig. 2 describe the authors' own integrated sensor module including soil humidity and temperature sensors at two depths.
rows.notes: The study describes soil moisture sensors at two levels used for closed-loop control, but reports no result on water use efficiency, targeted irrigation outcomes, or grapes (grapes are not mentioned). Only the precondition (sensor-based monitoring capability) is supported.

rows.evidence: Q1: Section III and Fig. 2 describe the authors' own sensor module with soil humidity sensors at two depths.
rows.notes: No crop quality or yield data of any kind; grapes are not mentioned. The paper only shows soil moisture monitoring was implemented in the system design, supporting a precondition rather than the claimed improvement in grape quality.

notes: Conference paper (Secrieru et al. 2017) describing the architecture, hardware and software of an autonomous drip/sprinkler irrigation control platform powered by wind/PV in Moldova. It contains no field experiment, no measured agronomic or water-use outcomes, no statistics; the only data shown is an example report diagram (Fig. 6). Q1 'yes' reflects own development/prototype work, but none of the five claims is supported by the study's own results.
